one_month_reasoning: No scheduled MP earnings in the window: Q2 was reported 2026-08-06, and Q3 is expected in early November, after 2026-10-30. The big policy dates also fall outside it. The expiry of China's suspension of its October 2025 export controls (2026-11-10) has effectively been pushed back: the US-China truce was extended to 2027-01-10 at the late-September Xi state visit, and the APEC meeting in Shenzhen is in November. Inside the window there is headline risk in both directions: thaw headlines have knocked rare-earth equities down 4-7% on single days; there are the Shenghe/China Rare Earth Group talks over a roughly 3% MP holder; and there are SMM NdPr price prints (about $97/kg, below the $110 DoD floor). The stock bounced 5.8% on 9/30 off a $44.75 low after falling from above $58. I see no edge on direction, so the ladder is a symmetric lognormal centered on $47.29 with about 19% monthly sigma (74%/3.5 = 21%, trimmed slightly because there is no earnings event).

fair_value.method: Blend of EV/EBITDA on forward EBITDA at the horizon (about 2028E $560M x 17x, less about $0.4B net debt, over about 200M fully diluted shares = $45.5) and forward P/E (NTM EPS at Sept 2027 about $1.40 x 35x = $49), weighted 50/50, gives about $47.5.

bear.story: A durable US-China deal at APEC/January extends or abolishes China's export controls, NdPr spot drifts to $70-80/kg and the scarcity premium collapses. The DoD floor protects Materials revenue, but the multiple compresses to 10-12x EBITDA, 10X slips, and Western magnet competitors (Vulcan 10kt, eVAC, Noveon, USAR) bid down the premium.

base.story: Truce rolls on with April 2025 heavy-RE licensing still in force. NdPr at $95-115/kg with the floor topping up, NdPr above 1,000t/qtr, magnet shipments ramp through 2027, and EBITDA moves toward $450-560M at a 16-18x multiple.

bull.story: Talks break down after 2027-01-10, China reimposes the expanded controls and the extraterritorial 0.1% rule, and NdPr goes above $130/kg (as in July 2026). Heavy RE separation and the gadolinium/defense offtake add value, the market pays for Western scarcity again, and the stock retests the $80-100 range.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $30 the market would be pricing MP near its floor-protected Materials value alone. That would most likely mean the 10X/magnet ramp has slipped badly or customer qualification failed, the DoD/Apple economics have been renegotiated, or a US-China settlement has durably erased the Western premium. Each of these breaks the integrated mine-to-magnet premium thesis, rather than reflecting ordinary 74%-vol noise.

reasoning: Industry evidence is mixed. Pricing: SMM NdPr oxide rose from about $53/kg in Jan 2026 to above $120 in July and fell back to about $97 in early September, so MP sits below its $110 DoD floor and is collecting PPA income ($17.6M in Q2). Competitor Lynas posted record FY26 results (revenue A$978M, NdPr about $101/kg by June) and signed a $110 floor with JARE, which confirms that Western floors are becoming standard; its shares still fell on the results, which signals a de-rating of the group. Policy: the sector sold off about 17-23% in a month on US-China thaw headlines, and the truce was extended to 2027-01-10 with rare earths unresolved; APEC Shenzhen in November is the next binary event. Competition: Vulcan Elements won the Army drone magnet supply and is building 10kt, and eVAC and Noveon are scaling. So MP's magnet scarcity premium is real but contested. On valuation, consensus 2027 EBITDA is $451.5M and EPS $0.87; rolled forward to horizon multiples, both methods give $45-49, close to the current $47.29, while sell-side targets average about $74 (anchor not used). Scenarios ($26/$50/$88 at 25/50/25) have a mean of about $53 and a median of about $48. I fitted a lognormal with a median of $48 and sigma 0.66, a little below the 74% realized vol because realized vol was inflated by the 2025-26 spike. Research was limited to about 12 queries/fetches; X/Twitter and prediction markets were not consulted.
